slides.title: Design and Human Evaluation of Tactile Withdrawal Reflexes for a Skin-Covered Robot Arm
slides.highlight: This research explores artificial nociception by mapping skin pressure to withdrawal motions, finding that predictable, uniform reflexes are perceived as more natural and safe by humans.

card.one_liner: A study comparing three tactile withdrawal reflexes for a skin-covered robot arm to evaluate human perception.
card.key_idea: A pipeline mapping skin pressure to 'pain gain' via a nonlinear model, triggering either uniform, bio-inspired location-dependent, or Cartesian-space withdrawal motions.
card.evaluation: Within-subject study with 15 participants using Godspeed scales and custom Likert items. Uniform reflexes were perceived as safest and most natural.
card.limitation: The embodiment gap between the robot and human arm may hinder the effectiveness of biologically inspired reflexes.

slides.title: τ: Learning Touch-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Models from Future Visual Supervision
slides.highlight: This framework integrates spatiotemporal tactile representations into Vision-Language-Action models using future visual supervision to improve manipulation robustness with limited data.

card.one_liner: τ is a touch-augmented VLA framework that learns tactile representations via future visual supervision.
card.key_idea: It uses a JEPA-style auxiliary branch to predict future visual feature changes from current tactile tokens and subsequent actions, aligning tactile representations with VLA semantic space.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on TacAura dataset across four contact-rich tasks; outperformed VLA and VTLA baselines, achieving up to 71.25% average success rate.
card.limitation: Generalization is task-dependent; precision-intensive tasks like USB insertion remain sensitive to object geometry variations and scene clutter.

slides.title: FeelWorld: Visuo-Tactile World Model for Hierarchical Contact Prediction and Planning
slides.tldr: VISUO-TACTILE WORLD MODEL FOR CONTACT-RICH PLANNING
slides.highlight: FeelWorld introduces a hierarchical world model that predicts visual latents alongside contact, force, and slip states to improve physical realism in imagined futures. It utilizes a contact-gated attention mechanism to enable robust zero-shot planning for tasks like grasping and insertion.

card.one_liner: FeelWorld is a visuo-tactile world model for contact-rich manipulation using hierarchical tactile state prediction and planning.
card.key_idea: A dynamics transformer predicting visual latents and hierarchical tactile states (contact, 3D latent, slip) using a contact-gated asymmetric attention mechanism to filter free-space sensor noise.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on chip grasping, fruit grasping, and USB insertion. Results show 81.7% average zero-shot planning success and improved LPIPS (0.058) over visual baselines.

slides.title: N0-TWAM: Scaling Tactile-Native World-Action Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: TACTILE-NATIVE WORLD-ACTION MODEL FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This research introduces a large-scale world-action model that predicts future vision and contact to improve fine-grained robotic manipulation.

card.one_liner: A large-scale world-action model that jointly predicts future vision and tactile signals for contact-rich manipulation.
card.key_idea: Uses an asymmetric Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) to predict future tactile/vision latents, while conditioning actions on both predicted foresight and observed force-space tactile representations.
card.evaluation: Tested on UniVTAC (84.5%), NeoSim (49.4%), and a real-robot suite (46.3%), outperforming VLA and vision-only world-action baselines.

slides.title: N0-VTLA: Scaling Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Model with Latent Tactile Tokens
slides.highlight: This work introduces N0-VTLA, a foundation model that integrates large-scale visuo-tactile pre-training and a predictive tactile pathway for fine-grained contact-rich manipulation.

card.one_liner: A vision-tactile-language-action model that predicts future tactile changes to improve contact-rich robotic manipulation.
card.key_idea: Uses a three-stage recipe to integrate a latent tactile predictor that conditions a flow-matching action expert on predicted future contact rather than current readings.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on NeoReal (9 real-robot tasks) and NeoSim (20 simulation tasks) against ACT and π0.5; outperformed baselines in both success rate and progress scores.

slides.title: Learning Personalized Safety Interventions for Haptic Human-Robot Shared Control
slides.highlight: This work proposes a Learning from Haptics framework to personalize safety interventions in shared control, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on human-AI intent alignment and adaptive coaching.

card.one_liner: A framework that learns personalized haptic safety interventions for robot teleoperation from sparse user demonstrations.
card.key_idea: It uses a differentiable Control Barrier Function (CBF)-QP layer to optimize safety response parameters, interpolating sparse user force preferences via Gaussian Process regression.
card.evaluation: Validated through AirSim hardware-in-the-loop simulations and real-world DJI Tello drone experiments using FPV and SDF-based constraints.

slides.title: ViTacWorld: Scaling Visuo-Tactile World Models for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
slides.tldr: SCALABLE VISUO-TACTILE WORLD MODEL FOR ROBOT MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: ViTacWorld introduces an action-conditioned world model that predicts visual and tactile feedback to synthesize rollouts and evaluate policies for contact-rich tasks.

card.one_liner: ViTacWorld generates action-conditioned visuo-tactile rollouts to scale data for contact-rich robot manipulation policies.
card.key_idea: An action-conditioned DiT world model pretrained on public and simulated visuo-tactile data, then finetuned with real rollouts using stream-aware modulation and cross-view attention.
card.evaluation: Tested on four contact-rich tasks using real-robot success rates; augmenting expert data with generated rollouts improved success rates (e.g., 42.5% to 67.5% for tactile policies).
card.limitation: Selection of successful 'dream data' for policy augmentation currently relies partly on manual inspection.

slides.title: FELT: Generating Tactile Signals from Vision for Visuo-Tactile Manipulation
slides.tldr: SYNTHESIZING TACTILE SIGNALS FROM RGB DATA
slides.highlight: FELT uses a visual encoder and query decoder to synthesize tactile images from RGB observations, reducing the need for scarce tactile data in contact-rich manipulation tasks.

card.one_liner: FELT synthesizes per-finger tactile pressure images from RGB observations to augment visuo-tactile manipulation policies.
card.key_idea: A frozen DINOv2 encoder and dual-branch attention decoder predict tactile signals, respecting sensor topology via separate finger branches and gated cross-panel information exchange.
card.evaluation: Tested on four contact-rich tasks using Diffusion Policies; FELT-generated signals and latent features improved success over vision-only baselines in real-robot trials.
card.limitation: Performance depends on paired data quality and requires visible contact regions; heavy occlusion can cause tactile inference failure.

slides.title: Generative Bionics Unveils Humanoid Robot with Full-Body Tactile Sensing
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOT WITH FULL-BODY TACTILE SENSING
slides.highlight: The development of a humanoid robot with full-body tactile sensing is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: LG Innotek and TDK Partnership for Robot Vision and Tactile Sensing
slides.tldr: ADVANCING ROBOT VISION AND TACTILE SENSING
slides.highlight: A partnership between LG Innotek and TDK aims to improve robot vision and tactile sensing capabilities.
